absent: Internal behavior of realtime spin, mutex and rw primitives beyond delegation names.
Full futex wait, wake, requeue, pi and vector wait queueing and timeout semantics.
Wound wait deadlock detection, wounding, rollback and slow path retry protocol.

findings.text: Realtime spinlock initialization prepares the embedded realtime base object and then applies lock dependency tracking setup with caller supplied name, key and per CPU marker. A secondary helper supplies a file local key and stringified lock name automatically. A local variant requests per CPU treatment.

Nested acquisition helpers exist in two build configurations. One configuration forwards subclass information to realtime aware nested primitives, validates an outer nesting lock dependency object before use, and reports zero interrupt flags while acquiring. The other configuration discards subclass information and forwards directly to normal spin acquisition including interrupt state saving.

Interrupt related spin acquisition and release helpers are annotated as acquiring and releasing the target lock. The disable path acquires the realtime lock and the enable path releases it, without separate interrupt masking behavior visible in these fragments.

Nonblocking spin acquisition is offered for normal, bottom half, interrupt and interrupt state saving contexts. The state saving form writes zero to caller flags before attempting acquisition. All forms return success or failure and are annotated as conditionally acquiring the lock only on success.

Contention query for this spin configuration always reports uncongested. Locked query reflects the state of the embedded realtime base object. An assertion helper traps when the lock is observed unlocked.

The generic spinlock object has two layouts. Without realtime support it contains a union holding either a raw spinlock or padding plus dependency map sized to the dependency map offset inside raw lock. With realtime support it contains a realtime base object plus an optional dependency map. Static constructors provide unlocked instances and a per CPU local unlocked variant.

A raw spinlock holds an architecture specific ticket, optional debug fields for magic, owner CPU and owner pointer, and an optional dependency map. Debug initialization uses a fixed magic signature, negative owner CPU and an all ones owner sentinel. Static constructors combine architecture unlocked state with debug and dependency initialization.

Dependency map static initialization assigns a stringified lock name and a wait classification. Raw locks request spin waiting, normal and local locks request configurable waiting, and local locks additionally mark per CPU type. All initializers expand to nothing when allocation debugging is disabled, as does debug initialization when spin debugging is disabled.

On single processor builds the architecture spin ticket is either a volatile unsigned word whose unlocked value is one or an empty structure with an empty unlocked initializer. The architecture read write ticket is an empty structure with an empty unlocked initializer and no debug variant.
Single processor architecture lock and unlock operations only order memory and ignore the lock argument. Contention query always reports uncongested.
Single processor architecture read and write lock primitives provide ordering only and no mutual exclusion, so callers must not rely on them for exclusion on that build.

A wound wait class holds a stamp counter, separate keys for acquire context and member mutexes, separate names for those keys, and a wait die selector. A member mutex holds a base mutex, a pointer to the current acquire context, and in debug builds a back pointer to its class. An acquire context holds owning task, stamp, acquired count, wounded and die mode flags, plus debug fields for completion, class and contending lock, lock dependency maps including a persistent first lock map, and optional deadlock injection controls.

The member mutex base type is selected by preemption mode. One build uses a normal mutex with normal init and locked query. The other uses a realtime mutex with realtime init and realtime base locked query.

Member mutex initialization initializes the base with class supplied name and key, clears current context, and in debug builds records the class. Destruction releases the base only on non realtime builds and requires the lock not held. Locked query delegates to the selected base locked test.

Acquire context lifecycle moves from init through optional done to fini. Init binds current task, allocates a unique stamp by relaxed increment of class stamp, clears acquired and wounded state, copies die mode, and acquires dependency tracking including a nested first lock map. Done requires the context held and marks acquisition complete while warning on duplicate completion. Fini releases dependency maps and poisons completion and acquired state so duplicate fini or unfinished use is detectable.

Slow acquisition wrappers require the acquire context held and in debug builds warn unless a contending lock is recorded. One wrapper performs uninterruptible acquisition and discards status, the other returns interruptible acquisition status. Both are annotated with corresponding acquire behavior on the member lock.

Wound wait debugging warns on duplicate acquire completion, on slow path use without a recorded contending lock, and on fini while locks remain acquired. Fini deliberately changes state so a second fini or use after fini is observable.

Futex base operations are numbered sequentially: wait zero, wake one, fd two, requeue three, compare requeue four, wake op five, lock pi six, unlock pi seven, trylock pi eight, wait bitset nine, wake bitset ten, wait requeue pi eleven, compare requeue pi twelve, lock pi two thirteen.

Futex flag bits are private 128, realtime clock 256, robust unlock 512, and 32 bit robust list 1024. The command mask preserves all bits except those four flags. Each listed private command combines its base operation with the private flag.

Robust unlock command aliases combine unlock or wake families with robust unlock and optionally private and 32 bit list selection, covering 64 and 32 bit pi unlock, wake list, and bitset list forms in both shared and private variants.

Second generation futex size field uses zero for 8 bit, one for 16 bit, two for 32 bit, three for 64 bit, with mask three. Additional option bits are NUMA four and memory policy eight. Private aliases the legacy private flag. The legacy 32 bit selector aliases the 32 bit size. No node is negative one. Maximum vector wait count is 128.

Vector wait entry contains expected value, user address, flags and reserved word in that order. Robust list node contains only a user pointer to next. Robust list head contains an embedded list node, a long offset from list node to futex field, and a user pending pointer used while a lock link is being established so termination can discover possibly held locks.

Futex word top bits are waiters high bit and owner died next bit, with remaining low 30 bits holding thread identity. Robust list traversal is bounded to 2048 entries. Robust mode modifier for pi is one and its mask currently contains only that bit.

Bitset match any is all ones. Wake operation codes are set zero, add one, or two, and not three, xor four, with a shift modifier bit at position eight meaning use one shifted by operand. Compare codes are equal zero, not equal one, less two, less equal three, greater four, greater equal five. The packed operation places operation in top four bits, comparison next four bits, operand in middle twelve bits and comparison argument in low twelve bits.

Global futex hashing uses read only after init mask, shift and bucket table plus an accessor returning the table as a runtime constant pointer. Private hash objects carry lifecycle state, hash mask, deferred free callback, owning memory descriptor, custom marker and trailing bucket array. Lifecycle state distinguishes per CPU reference mode from atomic reference mode.

Futex fault injection state pairs a fault attribute with an ignore private selector defaulting to false. A boot string hook forwards its argument to fault attribute setup. A predicate skips private faults when requested, otherwise consults the fault attribute once. An init hook publishes the fault attribute and boolean control under debugfs.

Private hash reference acquisition runs under a preemption guard and reads state once. Per CPU mode increments the caller CPU counter obtained through the owning memory descriptor and reports success. Atomic mode attempts an increment only if the atomic count is nonzero and reports its outcome.
